Text:
Nguyen Hue Walking Street offers a broad perspective on central Ho Chi Minh City. Along the view from City Hall towards the Saigon River, the square, surrounding façades and the everyday activity of pedestrians can be observed together.

Before it became a boulevard, this area was the Cho Vai canal. The canal was filled in 1887 to create a road. The pedestrian space opened to the public in April 2015. The tourism authority describes the square between Le Loi and Ton Duc Thang streets as a central pedestrian area with traffic continuing on both sides.

Try three viewpoints: look along the axis for its depth, sideways towards the façades, then nearby at how people use the square. The Ho Chi Minh monument near the City Hall end provides a recognisable reference. Observe from a suitable place without obstructing pedestrians.

Nguyen Hue illustrates changing uses of urban space: canal, boulevard and a pedestrian-focused public area. These stages connect historical dates to the present experience. Activities and arrangements can change during events, so follow current signs rather than assuming older photographs describe your visit.

Watch for traffic when leaving the esplanade for buildings or shops on either side, and cross at a suitable point. Keep the space clean, avoid stopping in pedestrian flows and consult organisers during events. Walking along the axis and looking back gives another perspective on the same place.
